edges.description: These host states favour invasive, bloodstream Salmonella infection rather than self-limited gastroenteritis.
Intestinal infection is the portal of entry for bloodstream invasion.
Intestinal infection causes diarrhoea, which has often resolved or never been noticed by the time the spinal infection presents.
Circulating Salmonella seeds the disc-endplate complex.
Bloodstream infection is detected as positive blood cultures.
Salmonella bacteremia can also seed the aortic wall, producing an infected native aortic aneurysm.
Seeded organisms establish infection in the disc-endplate niche.
Infection spreads from the aortic wall to the adjacent vertebral bodies and disc.
The aortic lesion is the clinical aneurysm.
Direct extension from the aortic wall infects the neighbouring discovertebral unit.
Local infection erodes the vertebral bodies on either side of the disc.
Discovertebral infection causes focal spinal pain.
Focal infection produces a systemic febrile response.
Focal infection drives a systemic acute-phase response.
Infection extends from the destroyed vertebrae into the epidural space, prevertebral tissue and psoas muscle.
Bone loss leads to vertebral collapse.
Epidural extension forms an abscess.
Paravertebral extension forms a psoas abscess.
Epidural abscess compressing the spinal cord can produce progressive paraplegia.
Intact cell-wall synthesis is needed for the bacterial growth that sustains the focal infection.
